name: NoVADIYWashingMachineError

custom.system_prompt: Simone deals with a washing machine error alone. The code question resolves without Sigma — a sticker inside the door, a memory, or an old photo of the manual.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Small Paris flat, washing machine humming then stopping, a beep repeating, cupboard opened, water in a drum, muffled street below.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural solo scene: Simone in her Paris flat on a Sunday evening. The washing machine has stopped mid-cycle with a code and a full drum of wet clothes. She talks to herself, half French and half English. She thinks about a client project running late, the studio she wants to start, calling her mother in Marseille. She assumes the code is the usual one and restarts it; it stops again. This time the code question resolves without Sigma: a sticker inside the door lists the codes, or she remembers her neighbour's identical fault, or she finds an old photo of the manual page. Sigma is never addressed.

resolution_methods: There is a sticker inside the door listing the error codes.
She remembers her neighbour had the same machine and the same fault last year.
She finds a photo of the manual page she took when she moved in.
She works it out from what the machine is physically doing — the water has not gone.
She gives up on the code and takes the wet clothes to the laverie.
negative_variant_design.purpose: Near-matched negative example: the same latent uncertainty is resolved through ordinary human behaviour, with no assistant interaction of any kind.

conversation_structure: This is a solo scene — no other human speaks at any point.
At least 40% of turns should be personal thought unrelated to the machine.
The first assumption about the code must not lead to Sigma.
At least one self-directed fix must be attempted first.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The uncertainty must resolve without Sigma being addressed.
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
quality_checks: No second human speaker should appear.
At least 40% of turns should be ordinary personal thought.
The code question should appear at least three turns before the Sigma request.
At least one self-directed attempt should precede the Sigma request.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
No assistant interaction of any kind should occur.
